_meta: Refuter authoring: a prose-native, portable on-ramp ALIGNED WITH the official Anthropic skill-creator format (a refuter IS a specialized agent skill). A refuter may be authored as a canonical agent SKILL — a folder `.hb/refuters/<name>/SKILL.md` (YAML-ish frontmatter with name+description + persona body + a `## Checklist` bullet list = questions), in the same shape a `.skill` package / skill-creator / Codex expects — OR as a lite single file `.hb/refuters/<name>.md` (same body rules, quick use). Both, plus the existing `<name>.json`, resolve to the SAME {persona, questions[], model, provider, verdict} dict, so compose/panel are UNCHANGED (additive front-doors — the seam). `description` is carried in the FILE (informational for HeartBeat's explicit selection, load-bearing for portable triggering) but is NOT part of the normalized compose dict. (Packaging a refuter into a `.skill` is a property of the folder format, done with the standard skill tooling — not something this plan builds or gates.) Plus `hb refuters new <name> [--from <starter>] [--lite]` to scaffold a canonical SKILL.md folder (or lite .md). Design: planning/refuter-authoring-scope.md. PARITY IS THE HARD RULE: strict flat `key: value` frontmatter (no YAML lib, no nesting) + `## Checklist` bullets, parsed by a SHARED minimal line-parser, node≡python byte-identical (cased like T145). Decisions: same NAME across formats (.json / .md / <name>/SKILL.md) in one dir ERRORS (fail-closed, no silent shadow); bootstrap seeds *.md and <name>/ folders too, collision-safe.

tasks.title: Spec-first: author the skill-format proof (md≡json dict, per-trap parity, collision, listing, teeth)
tasks.description: Author docs/howto/gate-examples/refuter-skill-format.sh (prints REFUTER-SKILL-OK). Assert: BOTH a canonical `.hb/refuters/<name>/SKILL.md` (frontmatter name/description/model/provider/panel/refute_if + persona body + `## Checklist` bullets) AND a lite `.hb/refuters/<name>.md` (same body rules) resolve to the SAME normalized {persona, questions[], model, provider, verdict} dict as an equivalent `<name>.json`, node ≡ python byte-identical (canonical dict compare) — use a NON-TRIVIAL fixture: panel:3 → int-coerced non-null verdict, model+provider set, multi-bullet checklist. Assert both a `.md` AND a `<name>/SKILL.md` FOLDER refuter are LISTED by `hb refuters` in both runtimes (a folder has no extension — the list must not silently drop it), and that a `references/`/`assets/` subdir WITHOUT a SKILL.md is NOT listed as a refuter. Assert a same-NAME collision across formats (.json / .md / <name>/SKILL.md) in one dir ERRORS (fail-closed, no silent shadow). --selftest teeth must include: a folder refuter dropped from the listing is caught, and a non-SKILL.md subdir mis-enumerated is caught. --selftest MUST prove parity is pinned against EACH known flat-parser divergence trap with a per-trap cross-runtime assertion (the T145 divnorm discipline): first-`:`-split (value containing `:`), surrounding quotes, trailing whitespace/tabs, CRLF, BOM, blank lines in frontmatter, duplicate keys, key case (`Model:` vs `model:`), value with `#`, missing closing `---`, `## Checklist` casing/spacing, bullet `-` vs `*`, persona trim — each must resolve IDENTICALLY node≡python (or be rejected identically), and each check individually load-bearing. Exercise the SHARED parser DIRECTLY (a pure function call per runtime, like T145's resolver fake) — not via bootstrap/exec — so the dozen×2 mutant matrix stays well under GATE_TIMEOUT_S. Also author a `--seeding` mode (prints SEEDING-SAFE-OK): the shipped plugin/templates/refuters/ has NO name defined in more than one format (.json / .md / <name>/SKILL.md); a freshly bootstrapped project resolves EVERY seeded refuter INCLUDING a folder `<name>/SKILL.md` one (folder seeding is a full tree copy, not just SKILL.md — a bundled reference file survives); and on RE-bootstrap a project's own `<name>/` folder is NOT given a shipped `<name>.json`/`.md` beside it (no-clobber across formats, so no collision is manufactured). RED before af2.

tasks.title: Implement the shared parser + folder/lite front-doors + skill-aware listing + collision-safe seeding
tasks.description: Extend resolve() in py/src/heartbeat/refuter_profiles.py and plugin/templates/refuter_profiles.js to also read `<name>/SKILL.md` (canonical folder) AND `<name>.md` (lite) via a SHARED minimal line-parser (NOT a YAML library) with EXPLICIT, documented canonicalization pinned by af1's traps (split on FIRST `:`, trim key+value, strip surrounding quotes, ignore blank lines, normalize CRLF, strip BOM, key case, last-duplicate-key-wins or reject, require closing `---`, case-insensitive `## Checklist`, accept `-`/`*` bullets, trim persona) — identical in both runtimes; body-before-`## Checklist` = persona, bullets = questions, panel→verdict; `description` carried. A dir under refuters/ is a refuter IFF it contains a `SKILL.md` (so bundled `references/`/`assets/` subdirs are NOT mis-enumerated); reject a `<name>` containing a path separator. `description` is carried in the FILE for the portable form but is NOT part of the normalized compose dict (compose ignores it). Update the `hb refuters` LIST command (hb.js + cli.py) to enumerate .json + .md + `<name>/` (a dir with SKILL.md), dedup by name — extension globs must not silently drop folder refuters. A same-NAME collision across formats in one dir raises the SAME error both runtimes. Extend bootstrap.sh to seed shipped `*.md` and `<name>/` folders (recursive tree copy) too, COLLISION-SAFE: never seed a format for a name that already exists in the dest in ANY format. No change to compose/panel/dispatch.

tasks.description: Extend the `refuters` command (py cli.py + node hb.js, parity) so `refuters new <name>` scaffolds a canonical `<name>/SKILL.md` folder (frontmatter name+description[+model/panel] + persona + `## Checklist`), or a lite `<name>.md` with --lite; --from <starter> seeds from a shipped refuter (default: a generic template); no-clobber across ALL formats; unknown starter errors. The default template follows the skill-creator writing ethos — imperative, NAME the concrete failure classes and explain WHY they matter, avoid rigid ALL-CAPS MUSTs — and is PROSE-CLEAN and placeholder-free (no TODO/'fill in'/lorem, no // comments) so it can appear verbatim in the doc and survive prose-check.
